prerequisites: Successful completion of modules from 1st and 2nd semesters as per study plan

learning_outcomes.text: Students are able to translate principle solutions into a spatial-material structure, considering essential boundary conditions, and design them for robust manufacturability.
They have internalized the 'tools' of constructive design and can apply them to develop successful products.
Furthermore, students master the fundamentals of Numerical Methods (NM) in an engineering context based on structural mechanics problems.
They are able to implement the application of NM using an FE program system proven in engineering practice.
They know the possibilities and limitations of NM, allowing them to apply the method meaningfully and critically evaluate analysis results.

syllabus_topics: Numerical methods (NM) for elastic truss, beam systems and plane problems of elasticity
Element types, element properties, element stiffness matrices and element and system stiffness relation
Initial stress and strain, distributed loads and equivalent node loads
Nodal point coordinates, rigid body and kinematical degrees of freedom, distributed element loads
Application of the NM to plane problems of stress and strain analysis

assessment_methods.method: Module final exam (Klausur or oral examination)

assessment_rules: The allocation of credit points occurs when the module final exam is passed. The exam duration is 120-150 minutes for a written exam or 45-60 minutes for an oral exam. In the exam, students should be able to reproduce, explain, and apply the essential fundamentals of constructive design and numerical methods in product development 1.
